linux.notes: Native Linux runtime probe on 2026-09-12: pinned v3.0.2 accepted the isolated -homedir/-ramdir/-keymapfile and complete -gamepad_reorder overlay, applied GAMEPAD=TRUE, loaded the selected gamecontrollerdb.txt, enumerated three SDL gamepads, and continued to the expected missing-ROM boundary. This proves parser/input initialization only; gameplay button behavior and NVRAM persistence remain unverified.

paths.naming: UNIX defaults to $HOME/.hypseus; input.cpp searches the home directory then application directory and creates the default INI.
With -gamepad or GLOBAL GAMEPAD=TRUE, lines are `KEY = key1 key2 pad0-button pad0-axis pad1-button pad1-axis`; values use source SDL_Gamepad macros or numeric values.
Games with NVRAM load/save compressed RAM under homedir/ram; short names are defined by each game driver.

controller_boundary.refusal: The adapter requires an exact saved framefile/runtime declaration, hashes every executable input, resolves physical devices through the target SDL3 build, writes only source-defined uppercase Gamepad macros into a private home, preserves NVRAM through an explicit external ram directory, and rejects custom environments, conflicting launch overrides, changed topology, or any command token beyond the source parser's 80-byte limit. The pinned native executable has accepted the generated parser/input overlay through SDL gamepad enumeration; gameplay button behavior and NVRAM persistence remain unverified.

linux-flatpak.reason: Upstream documents source builds and native Linux/Mac/Windows ports but publishes no first-party Flatpak artifact; a separately verified package and sandbox paths are required.
